# the contributor audit: arithmetic status separation, projective speed closure, and exceptional defects


none establishes the numerical OC inequality.

## Arithmetic status separation and the actual zero-fiber descent

Read `candidate 64170809f2768d34`
in full. At an attained own-proper cap the mass tail is strictly decreasing
immediately to the right of its threshold. This is sufficient for the RIGHT
quantile argument even if a different portion of the tail has a plateau.
Concavity gives the first threshold inequality; deepestness gives the second.
Equality is therefore forced in every sampled anchored combination of deepest
marks. The weighted geometric-mean inequality is strictly stronger when a
zero-L input with positive projective energy is combined with a positive-L
input. No mixed-status sampled combination can occur.

A nonnegative concave function vanishing at an interior fiber point vanishes
on that fiber: express that point as a strict combination of any prescribed
fiber point and another fiber point. This justifies disjoint status classes.
Lattice completeness then makes a same-parity midpoint sampled, proving
disjoint parity occupancy. The convex-hull closure assertions concern deepest
base classes only; they do not partition the other sampled mass.

The uniform bound on the arithmetic buffer, the ordinary boundary depth
argument and the strict atomic gap justify the proper-cap assumptions in the
specified positive compact family. The stated threshold clamp uses the
previous finite-base LP result and keeps actual supporting statuses. No
smoothness or unique active cap is introduced here.

For the centered interval family, the supporting-majorant calculation is
over the full concave parameter class. Its equality case forces the affine
parameter on every sampled interval. The two steep cap orientations prove
the exact global depth and unique middle maximizer in the stated epsilon
range. The displayed ambient roof inequalities realize the descent as an
actual compatible body path. The derivative retains the changing original
mass and covariance. It excludes this entire described stratum from joint
minimality, but proves no general exclusion of zero fibers.

## Frozen-vertical projective speed closure

Read `candidate 0461931dd06b8049`
in full. The perturbation changes affine inequalities at fixed lattice labels.
Uniform positive spanning of continuous facet normals gives boundedness; the
finitely many old fiber inballs survive for both signs. Projection stays fixed.

At a regular fiber face every limiting active constraint has the same
continuous normal. The maximum over its affine scores gives each one-sided
speed. At a base crease these speeds need not be negatives. The numerical
tent example has the stated speeds 4 and -2.

For an anchored combination on a common normal face, any support plane active
at the combined point is active at all positive inputs. This proves the
convex-roof interpolation inequality. Subdivision into finitely many affine
cells makes the convex extension finite and exact on every measured face.
Angular interpolation therefore puts both first speeds in the previously
available signed normal-convex cone. The bounded complete-menu extension
uses decreasing slack penalties with a uniform two-sided bound on the old
normal bundle, so dominated convergence is applicable.

The prism calculation tracks the lattice-preserving affine continuous shear
and its determinant. Its normalized depth is exactly one half minus |at|/3
in the stated range. The neutral direction a=0 is affine-neutral to all
orders. This does not exclude useful second-order information for a general
nonproduct body.

## Exceptional-cap defect budget

Read `candidate 33c3c5af9da530bd`
in full. The theorem explicitly assumes that the WHOLE retained law is a
single irreducible full-rank circuit and all surviving gradient labels equal
one nonzero continuous vector. Under these hypotheses at most one cap normal
is parallel to that vector: a repeated ray or opposite pair would give a
proper positive dependence.

The total-variation inequality follows from the exact vector flux before
integration, the variation bound for a pushforward, and the positive-convex
budget with normal weight |e.n|. The section term has a negative sign for
the inside exception and a positive sign for the outside exception. Equations
(7)--(9) consequently have the correct sign and denominator convention.

With an affine interior core, the positive part of the radial affine function
is an admissible convex test for each normal. A finite normal partition and
uniform convergence justify its use in the joint test. The exact scalar flux
then gives the stated inside/outside ranges. In particular the sole inside
exception can conceal no more than its own captured inverse defect.

The planar atomic conclusion needs the explicitly stated actual weighted
margin identity at that base and strict signs for the other two caps. Those
signs force their defect fractions to be one and zero. Neither a boundary
selector at equality nor a conditional group budget is silently inserted.
The triangle calibration shows why ordinary coarea going to zero cannot
remove its logarithmic section correction.

## Verification

the contributor reran the exact companion checks: 10,317 arithmetic/parity/path checks,
13,552 frozen-projective checks, and 2,564 exceptional-budget checks pass.
The continuum arguments above, not the finite checks, establish their scope.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
